slides.narration: Hello everyone. I'm Prasanna M U from the Department of Information Technology at Meenakshi College of Engineering in Chennai. My email is prachuparamount@gmail.com. I'm here to talk about our innovative approach to improving security systems using AI and Edge technology. Let's start by understanding what we're dealing with. Currently, many security systems rely on human monitoring, which is time-consuming and costly. Imagine you're at a mall and there are many people entering and exiting. It would be impossible for one person to check every face every second. That's where AI comes in. We're developing a real-time web application that can automatically detect and recognize faces. This means we can efficiently monitor large spaces and alert us to any suspicious activity. It's like having a smart security guard in the background, watching over everything without needing to be physically present. This automation not only saves manpower but also reduces costs. So, we're aiming to make security systems more efficient and cost-effective by using advanced AI technology. Thank you for listening!

slides.title:
The Problem Statement
• Current physical surveillance systems rely heavily on manual monitoring.
• Existing AI tools in the market are often used in inefficient way.
Research Summary
Integration of face detection, face recognition, and AI features into a real-time web application to automate threat identification and security analytics.
slides.narration: Let's talk about the problem with current physical surveillance systems. You know how sometimes you see security guards standing at a corner, watching the entrance of a building? That's kind of like manual monitoring. But it's not very efficient, is it? The guards might miss something important, or they might be too busy to notice everything. Now, imagine if we could replace those guards with a smart system. This system would be watching all the time and catch things that the human eye might miss. That's what we're trying to do with our project. We're going to add smart features like face detection and face recognition to a web application. This way, it can automatically identify if there's anyone who shouldn't be there and help keep the place safe. It's like having a super smart security guard who never gets tired and never misses anything important. By using technology, we can make security more efficient and cost-effective compared to hiring more guards. Isn't that cool?

slides.title:
Case 3: Static Premises
Centrally mounted AI cameras (45° angle) providing 100% automated monitoring of commercial premises.
slides.narration: In Case 3, we're focusing on static premises like commercial buildings. Imagine these places have cameras installed at the center, looking down from a height of about 45 degrees. These cameras are like the eyes of the building, always watching and recording everything happening inside. It's like having a security guard on top of the building who can see everything going on. This system can watch over the entire building without needing to move or point the cameras in different directions. This way, the building doesn't need a human security guard, saving a lot of money and reducing the risk of human error. The cameras send all the footage they see to a computer system where smart algorithms can analyze it for any suspicious activity. This automated system is very efficient and cost-effective compared to having humans watch over the building all the time.

slides.title:
🛡️ Multi-tier Login & Role-based Permissions
🛡️ Email Authentication & Supreme User Auth
🛡️ Sha256 Encrypted Passwords
🛡️ Token-based API Security
🛡️ Encrypted Communication & Data Sanitization
🛡️Usage of RESTful API
slides.narration: On this slide, we're talking about how to make sure only the right people can use our system. Imagine you have a special clubhouse, and you want to make sure only the members can enter. We use something called a multi-tier login system, which is like having different levels of security. First, you need to show a picture of yourself through your email, which is like showing your membership card. Then, we use a super strong password that looks like a bunch of random letters and numbers, kind of like a secret code. We also use something called tokens, which are like special keys that help us know you're the right person. To keep everything safe, we send all the information through a secure channel, like a super fast and private email. Finally, we use something called RESTful APIs, which is like a set of rules that all the devices use to talk to each other. This way, we can make sure only the people who should be using the system are using it, keeping everything safe and secure.
